title: Kiosk blocked-item status
lede: When a scanned item cannot be added, the counter operator can now see who has it, what kind of hold it is, and when it is due back.

stats.n: Reserved and Checked Out are distinct from generic conflicts
Person, item, and local due-back time

sections.heading: Checkout scan stage
sections.note: Same availability-conflicts fixture, same cart, same iPad Air 11-inch (M4) simulator viewport.

pairs.title: When adding the item is blocked
pairs.sub: Read the banner and the first two cart rows.
pairs.beforeCap: The source baseline collapsed both reservation and active checkout into generic Conflict labels, with no owner or deadline in the scan feedback.
pairs.afterCap: The rejected-add feedback says “Erik Role has reserved the FX3 2 until Sep 12 at 4:30 PM”; the cart also distinguishes Reserved from Checked Out.

changes.was: A blocked serialized item surfaced only generic unavailable/conflict copy, so the operator could not tell who had the camera or when it would return.
changes.now: The server includes optional requester, booking-kind, and status metadata; the Kiosk turns that into a direct person/item/deadline message and preserves a safe fallback for older responses.

changes.h: Reservation and active custody now read differently
changes.was: A reservation and an open checkout looked the same in the scan cart.
changes.now: Reserved, Checked Out, and Pending Pickup use state-specific labels, semantic status colors, and matching VoiceOver/accessibility text.

verification: Focused behavior and source-contract tests: 48/48 passing, including reservation and active-checkout copy.
Web gates: TypeScript, ESLint, and npm run build:app pass.
Native gates: WisconsinKiosk Debug and Release simulator builds pass; iOS project parity, drift, and gap audits pass.
Visual: matched baseline and final captures were inspected on the available iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5 simulator.
notes: This is local source/build proof only. The production deployment and authenticated managed-iPad/scanner acceptance gate remain open.

The Kiosk target has no dedicated UI-test target in the current project, so the repeatable DEBUG fixture was launched with simctl after native compilation; no live credentials or production data were used.
Repository docs verification still reports generated codemap drift. The pre-existing dirty codemap was preserved rather than regenerated over parallel work.
